evidence.quote: 1803, variant of {{m|en|stamp}}. Compare {{cog|de|stampfen||to stomp}}. More at {{l|en|stamp}}.

"lively social dance" is recorded by 1912 in jazz slang. Stompers "large, heavy shoes" is… See origin and meaning of stomp. from Old English stempan "to pound, crush, or bruise in or as in a mortar," from Proto-Germanic *stamp- (source also of Old Norse stappa , Danish stampe , Middle Dutch stampen , Old High German stampfon , German stampfen "to stamp with the foot, beat, pound," German Stampfe "pestle"), from nasalized form of PIE root *stebh- "to support, place firmly on" (source also of Greek stembein "to trample, misuse;" see staff (n.
